meta.title: Esophageal cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Esophageal and gastroesophageal-junction cancer (Siewert I-II), adult
meta.population: Adults with esophageal or GEJ cancer - one spec whose spine is the HISTOLOGY FORK: squamous and adenocarcinoma are different diseases wearing one organ, with different geographies, different radiotherapy sensitivity, different 1L receipts, and now different perioperative verdicts. The SIEWERT HANDOFF completes the gastric row's boundary from the other side: type I is this trainer's (CROSS, KEYNOTE-590 enrolled it by name), type III reroutes LIVE to the gastric trainer, and type II is carried here (CROSS/ESOPEC/CheckMate 577 covered it) while honestly CONTESTED - the gastric perioperative trials (FLOT4, MATTERHORN) enrolled GEJ too, and the two rows say the same thing about the shared zone.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where two standards finally fought head-to-head and one won. THE ESOPEC VERDICT is the headline: in resectable esophageal ADENOCARCINOMA, perioperative FLOT beat CROSS trimodality directly - median OS 66 vs 37 months (HR 0.70, p=0.012, NEJM 2025) - and the trainer renders the verdict the honest way: BOTH cards stay on the adenocarcinoma menu, FLOT ranking on its verified 66, CROSS ranking on the 37 the trial it lost measured live (its own 2012 number, 49.4 months, came from a 75%-adeno mixed cohort and stays on the squamous card where CROSS…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC TNM 8th; squamous vs adenocarcinoma as the load-bearing split; Siewert classification at the junction (I here / III gastric / II contested - both rows say so); PD-L1 scored two ways (CPS for pembrolizumab, TPS for nivolumab - the two-ruler honesty); NCCN Esophageal/EGJ v3.2026 (secondhand - 403)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for advanced disease; clinical complete response after chemoradiation is read by the preSANO protocol (bite-on-bite biopsies + EUS-FNA + PET-CT) - the read that makes active surveillance a discussable road; pathologic residual disease after trimodality is the ticket CheckMate 577's adjuvant door requires

Newly diagnosed.name: Perioperative FLOT + esophagectomy (ESOPEC - the verdict's winner)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the resectable-adenocarcinoma standard by head-to-head verdict (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the four-drug regimen around a major operation - cytopenias and neuropathy, then the permanent eating change
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the gland-type cancer that can be operated on: strong chemotherapy before and after the operation - the road that beat the older radiation-first road when the two were finally compared directly, by more than two years of median survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: CROSS trimodality in adenocarcinoma (the beaten road, measured live)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the former co-standard, now second by verdict (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (CROSS) + live measurement (ESOPEC's control arm)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemoradiation's esophagitis and counts, then the operation
Newly diagnosed.patient: The older standard - chemotherapy with radiation, then the operation - still real, now honestly ranked second for the gland-type cancer after losing the direct comparison.

Newly diagnosed.name: CROSS trimodality in squamous disease (the standing standard)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: esophagitis and counts through CRT, then the operation's ledger
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the squamous type that can be operated on: chemotherapy with radiation, then the operation - the proven standard, with one in three patients alive at ten years versus one in four with surgery alone.

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant nivolumab after trimodality (CheckMate 577 - approved ON disease-free survival)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved 2021-05-20 ON DFS (secondhand) - the currency named on the card
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - DFS decisive, mature OS NS at ASCO 2025 abstract level (DFS-labeled: displays, never ranks)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a year of the immune watch-list on top of post-surgical recovery
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the operation's pathology finds cancer still present after chemoradiation: a year of immunotherapy - approved on proof that it keeps cancer away longer, with the longer-life question now read out and honestly unproven, and the card says exactly that.

Newly diagnosed.name: Active surveillance after clinical CR (SANO - organ preservation at its honest grade)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: emerging option, experienced centers, trial-grade surveillance (not yet standard - said so)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 cluster-randomized noninferiority at 2 years (labeled: displays, never ranks; maturity pending)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: no operation unless regrowth - the cost is vigilance: the surveillance schedule IS the treatment
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the careful post-radiation check finds no remaining cancer: watching closely instead of operating - keeping the esophagus - looked as safe as surgery at two years in the trial that tested it, and the honest fine print is that two years is still young evidence.
drugs: Active surveillance per SANO protocol (salvage surgery on regrowth)

Newly diagnosed.name: Definitive chemoradiation, 50.4 Gy (the third tine's own road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the unresectable/inoperable curative-intent standard (NCCN secondhand); dose fixed by two trials
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized legacy (RTOG 85-01) + two verified negative dose-escalation trials; the 5-yr percentage flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: esophagitis is the named cost - intake support through the radiation weeks is treatment-preserving
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the tumor can't be operated on but hasn't spread: chemotherapy with radiation given to cure - a real curative road, not a consolation - at the radiation dose two separate trials proved is enough.

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemo-immunotherapy, 1L squamous (CheckMate 648 / RATIONALE-306)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the 1L metastatic-squamous standard (NCCN secondhand; three approved anti-PD-1 partners)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (648 verified, 306 verified) - OS met in both
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemo's ledger plus the immune one
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread squamous-type disease: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy - proven to extend life in two separate trials, more so when the tumor carries the immune marker.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pembrolizumab + chemo, 1L adenocarcinoma/Siewert I (KEYNOTE-590)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemo's ledger plus the immune one
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread gland-type disease of the esophagus or upper junction: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy - the proven opener, with tumor tests first because some results open stronger doors borrowed from the stomach-cancer playbook.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; the swallowing-and-intake craft is the care
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - with a team whose craft centers on swallowing, comfort, and eating for pleasure where possible.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Nivolumab 2L squamous, IO-naive (ATTRACTION-3 - the receipt with a flagged citation)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met (numbers concordant; primary PMID flagged, 3-yr paper matched)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the immune ledger alone - gentler than the taxane it beat
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For squamous-type disease after platinum chemotherapy, if immunotherapy hasn't been used yet: immunotherapy alone - it beat chemotherapy on survival and is gentler.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Chemotherapy 2L+ (the measured bar; the junction reaches across)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized control-arm measurement (ATTRACTION-3's own arm) + the KEYNOTE-181 CPS>=10 receipt (HR flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The proven later-line chemotherapy - and for junction gland-type tumors, the stomach-cancer playbook's stronger doors may apply instead, tumor tests deciding.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after the proven lines is a real road - and this card carries the field's honest ledger: several hoped-for drug combinations were tested properly and did not work, and the trainer names them rather than hiding them.

van Hagen et al. CROSS: preoperative chemoradiotherapy (carbo/paclitaxel + 41.4 Gy) + surgery vs surgery - median OS 49.4 vs 24.0 (HR 0.657, CI 0.495-0.871, p=0.003; n=366 analyzed; 75% adeno / 23% SCC - the mixed cohort said). NEJM 2012 (PMID 22646630, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 22646630 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25
Eyck et al. CROSS 10-year: OS 38% vs 25%; cancer-specific death HR 0.60 (0.46-0.80). J Clin Oncol 2021 (PMID 33891478, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 33891478 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Hoeppner et al. ESOPEC: perioperative FLOT vs CROSS trimodality, resectable esophageal ADENOCARCINOMA head-to-head (n=438) - median OS 66 vs 37 (HR 0.70, CI 0.53-0.92, p=0.012); 3-yr 57.4% vs 50.7% (5-yr 50.6% vs 38.7% secondhand follow-up). THE VERDICT. NEJM 2025 (PMID 39842010, pubmed-url-match; LOOKALIKE HAZARD: PMID 42377661 is a similarly titled meta-analysis - not cited) | PMID 39842010 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Kelly et al. CheckMate 577: adjuvant nivolumab after trimodality with residual pathologic disease - median DFS 22.4 vs 11.0 (HR 0.69 - CI soft-flagged, not independently re-verified). FDA 2021-05-20 ON DFS (secondhand; approval summary PMID 35960160 matched). NEJM 2021 (PMID 33789008, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 33789008 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

CheckMate 577 mature OS (ASCO 2025, ABSTRACT-LEVEL - no peer-reviewed OS paper found): median OS 51.7 vs 35.3, HR 0.85 (0.70-1.04), p=0.1064 - NOT significant in ITT; 5-yr OS 46% vs 41%; benefit enriched CPS>=1; 5-yr DFS 21.8 vs 10.8 (HR 0.76). The spec never claims OS benefit proven

Doki et al. CheckMate 648: 1L advanced ESCC (n=970, 1:1:1) - nivo+chemo vs chemo: OS 13.2 vs 10.7 (HR 0.74, p=0.002); TPS>=1%: 15.4 vs 9.1 (HR 0.54, p<0.001); nivo+ipi arm 12.7 all-comers (exact HR soft-flagged). TPS not CPS - the two-ruler note. FDA both regimens 2022-05-27 (secondhand). NEJM 2022 (PMID 35108470, pubmed-url-match; 29-mo follow-up PMID 38716626 matched) | PMID 35108470 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Sun et al. KEYNOTE-590: 1L esophageal (both histologies) + SIEWERT TYPE I GEJ adenocarcinoma by name - pembro+chemo: all-patients OS 12.4 vs 9.8 (HR 0.73, 0.63-0.86); CPS>=10: 13.5 vs 9.4 (HR 0.62, 0.49-0.78). FDA 2021-03-22 (secondhand). Lancet 2021 (PMID 34454674, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 34454674 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

RATIONALE-306: tislelizumab + chemo, 1L advanced ESCC (n=649) - OS 17.2 vs 10.6 (HR 0.66, 0.54-0.80, p<0.0001). FDA 1L ESCC PD-L1>=1 2025-03 (secondhand). Lancet Oncol 2023 (PMID 37080222, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 37080222 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Herskovic et al. RTOG 85-01: CRT (50 Gy + cis/5-FU) vs RT 64 Gy alone - the definitive-CRT road's founding receipt. NEJM 1992 (PMID 1584260, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 1584260 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Cooper et al. RTOG 85-01 long-term follow-up - the classic ~26% vs 0% 5-year OS figures carried as FLAGGED (paper PMID-matched; the percentages not independently re-verified this sweep). JAMA 1999 (PMID 10235156, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 10235156 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Minsky et al. INT 0123/RTOG 94-05: 64.8 vs 50.4 Gy definitive CRT - no benefit to escalation; 50.4 Gy stands. THE DOSE LESSON, first telling. J Clin Oncol 2002 (PMID 11870157, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 11870157 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Hulshof et al. ARTDECO: 61.6 Gy boost vs 50.4 Gy definitive CRT (n=260, 61% SCC) - no local-control or survival gain. THE DOSE LESSON, second telling. J Clin Oncol 2021 (PMID 34101496, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 34101496 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

SANO: active surveillance vs standard surgery after cCR to nCRT (stepped-wedge cluster-randomized noninferiority; cCR n=309) - 2-yr OS 74% vs 71% (HR 1.14, CI 0.74-1.78; 15% margin met). Noninferior AT 2 YEARS, maturity pending, methodology debated in live correspondence (secondhand) - an emerging option, not a standard. Lancet Oncol 2025 (PMID 40112851, pubmed-url-match; LOOKALIKE HAZARD: PMID 41725589 is a German-language secondary version - not cited) | PMID 40112851 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Noordman et al. preSANO: bite-on-bite biopsies + EUS-FNA + PET-CT for residual-disease detection after nCRT - the named protocol that defines a real cCR read. Lancet Oncol 2018 (PMID 29861116, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 29861116 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Kato et al. ATTRACTION-3: nivolumab vs taxane, 2L ESCC post-platinum - OS 10.9 vs 8.4 (HR 0.77, 0.62-0.96, p=0.019; n=419). CITATION FLAGGED: the primary PMID (31582355) never surfaced as a pubmed URL this sweep - the ADJACENT PMID 31582356 is the journal's COMMENT with a near-identical title (the trap class, caught again; wrong-PMID catch #27); numbers concordant across sources, receipt carried by the matched 3-yr paper. Lancet Oncol 2019 (PMID FLAG) | PMID 31582355 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

ATTRACTION-3 3-year follow-up: OS 15.3% vs 8.7% - the matched paper carrying the receipt. Clin Cancer Res 2022 (PMID 35294546, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 35294546 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Kojima et al. KEYNOTE-181: pembrolizumab vs chemo, 2L advanced esophageal - CPS>=10: OS 9.3 vs 6.7 (HR FLAGGED - commonly quoted 0.69, not independently re-verified). Largely pre-1L-IO era. J Clin Oncol 2020 (PMID 33026938, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 33026938 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

THE GRAVEYARD (all secondhand, dated, named honestly): STAR-221 (domvanalimab+zimberelimab+chemo, 1L HER2-neg GEA) DISCONTINUED for futility by IDMC - OS 14.0 vs 13.4, no benefit even PD-L1-high; registry record COMPLETED 2026-08-28 actual (REGISTRY FIRSTHAND 2026-09-07) - closure of the discontinued study, not a readout; SKYSCRAPER-07 (tira+atezo post-dCRT unresectable ESCC) FAILED - tira+atezo numerically worse than atezo alone (ESMO 2025), Roche scrapped the tiragolumab esophageal program 2025-07; LEAP-014 (lenvatinib+pembro+chemo 1L ESCC) stopped early for futility - OS 17.6 vs 15.5, NS (ESMO 2025, no PMID found). KEPT DISTINCT: KEYNOTE-975 and KUNLUN (dCRT+IO) are closed-AWAITED, not failed - readouts pending, re-check weekly. EA2174: neoadjuvant nivo NEGATIVE (no pCR gain, ASCO 2024), adjuvant randomization readout PENDING

THE PENDING SHELF (pointer - the gastric row carries the card-level detail): zanidatamab APPROVED 2026-08-25 (1L HER2+ GEA, both regimens; triplet IHC 3+ or 2+/ISH+, chemo doublet IHC 3+ only). HERIZON-GEA-01 primary = NEJM 2026;394:2002-14, PMID 42202319 (pubmed-abstract-match, flag RESOLVED 2026-08-26): PFS 12.4 vs 8.1 (HR 0.63); OS 26.4 vs 19.2 (HR 0.72, P=0.004); doublet interim OS NOT significant (HR 0.80, P=0.06). Existing zanidatamab approval is biliary (2024-11, secondhand)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
